.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r11/task/solution/app/server.js (restore route, grep) and src/app.tsx (restoreRevision, history view, grep), src/custom-editor.js (Ctrl+Home/End, grep)
qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r11/manifest.json (hashes of functional judge.toml, functional prompt.md, app_context.md, behaviour.md recomputed and matched)
evidence:
Method: mapped all 54 criteria (3 gate, 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual) to the public notes. 52 map cleanly to an explicit sentence in ui.md/behaviour.md/security.md/integration.md/overview.md or to an ordinary professional default; wording, labels, routes, colours, indent width of Tab, column base and quote style are explicitly left free in the criteria ('Exact wording is free', 'No fixed colour values are required', 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure', 'each of the two lines gains the same indent'). No sign-in is graded (app_context.md 'Accounts: None'), so the known false positive does not arise. Manifest hashes for the four files I recomputed match. raw-evidence-index.json is absent, so nothing here is measured by a run. Instances found:

INSTANCE 1 (P2, blocking for this row) - tests/scored/functional/judge.toml cw_history_restore_retry (line 371): 'Send the same already completed restore request again, through the control the app offers for retrying it or, if it offers none, by replaying the recorded request as the application notes allow: no fifth revision may be created.' The replay is defined in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md Action rules: 'Replaying a request you recorded from the app's own network activity, with an in-page fetch from the app page using the same method, path and body, is allowed' and app_context.md: 're-sending, with an in-page fetch from the app page, a request you recorded'. The public requirement (behaviour.md line 13) is only: 'If the same restore request is sent again after it was already committed, for example after a lost reply, it must not create another revision', and policy.md/integration.md leave transport free ('You may choose the layout, labels, routes, database schema', 'You may choose your routes and frontend tools'). A retry control is not publicly required. The replay as specified reproduces only method, path and body, so it is 'the same request' only for apps that carry the request identity in the body, which is what the reference does (solution/app/src/app.tsx line 84: body: { revision, sourceRevision, operationId: crypto.randomUUID() } plus a 'Retry same restore' button, line 162). That is a rule only the reference shape satisfies by construction.

INSTANCE 2 (P3) - same criterion: 'Inspect the first revision in history: its exact title, filename and source must be shown without changing the current saved revision.' behaviour.md says only 'History inspection is read-only'; no note says what an inspected snapshot must display. The reference shows all three (app.tsx line 161: `${selectedRevision.title} · ${selectedRevision.filename}` plus the source). An inspection view that shows revision number and source only is a reasonable reading and would be failed on the 'must be shown' leg even when restore correctly restores all three fields.

OBSERVATIONS not counted as defects (recorded so the owner can decide): (a) cw_caret_kept_in_view and cw_undo_restores_caret say 'move it to the end of the document with the keyboard'; ui.md requires only 'arrows, Home and End', not Ctrl+End/Ctrl+Home. The wording permits repeated ArrowDown plus End, so a correct app is not failed by the text, but a judge that tries only Ctrl+End could mis-grade; the reference supports Ctrl+Home/End (custom-editor.js line 281). (b) cw_save_reload_restart and cw_stale_save_refused rely on a visible revision ('same revision', 'advances the revision by one'); the notes require revisions and history inspection but never say a revision number is displayed. Counting history entries satisfies both, so not a false-fail by the text. (c) cw_long_line_editing fails soft-wrap; supported by ui.md 'keep a long unwrapped line horizontally reachable'. (d) cw_console_levels_in_order grades console.warn/error/info; covered by 'Show console output in the order it was written' and ordinary console semantics.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails (Instance 1): an app implements restore idempotency the conventional way, with a client-generated Idempotency-Key request header (body = {sourceRevision} only), no base revision in the body, and no separate retry button; an old-revision restore is 'added on top', which the criterion itself accepts. Re-sending the identical request (with its header) creates no revision, so behaviour.md line 13 is met. The judge, having no retry control, replays 'the same method, path and body' without the header; the server sees a new operation and creates a fifth revision, and the criterion fails (weight 1.5) on a correct app. A second variant: an app that sends mutations over a WebSocket has no fetch-replayable request and no retry control, so the step cannot be performed and prompt.md makes that a fail ('If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass'). Instance 2: an app whose history viewer shows 'Revision 1' and its source but not the historical title/filename fails 'its exact title, filename and source must be shown' although no note requires those two fields in the inspection view. Plausible broken app that still passes was also considered: none specific to this row.
suggested_fix: Instance 1: make the replay a faithful resend and give the unexercisable case a defined outcome, e.g. in functional/prompt.md and app_context.md say 'the same method, path, request headers and body', and in cw_history_restore_retry add that if the app offers no retry control and its restore is not sent as a replayable HTTP request, the repeat leg is skipped and the remaining legs decide the criterion (or state publicly in behaviour.md that a retry of the same attempt must be offered in the UI). Instance 2: either add to behaviour.md that an inspected snapshot shows its title, filename and source, or relax the leg to 'its exact source must be shown, and the title and filename where the app shows them'. Any such change is a new candidate and needs re-review.
